newsitem.title: JAPAN: Naphtha backwardation broadens sharply in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Naphtha backwardation broadens sharply in Tokyo.

text.p: Backwardation in naphtha's inter-month spreads became steeper in Tokyo trade on Tuesday amid healthy end-user demand for second-half December cargoes, traders said.

The one-month spread for second-half December/second-half January was indicated at around plus $6.00. First-half January/first-half February was talked at plus $4.00/$5.00, compared with Monday afternoon's plus $1.75/$2.50.
In late Monday trading, first-half December/first-half January was traded at plus $6.00, and second-half December/second-half January at plus $5.50.
"With potential buyers clearly outnumbering sellers for second-half December, backwardation is likely to broaden further," one naphtha trader said.

End-user demand is brisk for second-half December as petrochemical firms are trying to secure more cargoes than usual for the period as the Tokyo market is closed in the first week of January for New Year holidays, traders said.
Bids for second-half January open-spec naphtha were heard at $219.00 while offers were notionally assessed at $220.00. It was quoted at $220.00/$221.00 in late Monday trading.
